title: Accessible Tables & Forms 📊
description: Build data tables and forms that are easy to understand, navigate, and complete.

slides.title: Data Tables: Not Just for Layout 🗄️
slides.content:
Tables should only be used for **tabular data**, never for layout.

* Use `<table>` with proper structure: `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<th>` for headers.
* Scope attribute helps screen readers associate headers with cells.
* Add a `<caption>` for context.

Screen readers can navigate tables cell‑by‑cell, announcing row/column headers.

quizData.question: What does the `scope` attribute on a `<th>` do?

options.text: Indicates whether it's a column or row header

quizData.explanation: `scope='col'` or `scope='row'` helps assistive tech associate header cells with data cells.

slides.title: Forms: The Conversation 💬
slides.content:
Forms are how users communicate with your site. Every input needs a **label** – properly associated.

* Use `<label for="input-id">` – explicit association.
* Or wrap the input inside `<label>` – implicit association (less robust).
* Placeholder text is **not** a label – it disappears and has low contrast.
* Group related fields with `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`.

slides.title: Explicit Label Example
slides.codeSnippet:
<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>

quizData.question: What happens when you click on a `<label>` correctly associated with an `<input>`?
quizData.explanation: Clicking a label focuses its associated input, increasing the touch target and usability.

slides.title: Fieldsets & Legends 🧩
slides.content:
For groups of radio buttons or checkboxes, wrap them in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`.

* `<legend>` acts as the label for the entire group.
* Screen readers announce the legend for each option in the set.
* Example: shipping options group.

slides.title: Radio Group Example
slides.codeSnippet:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Preferred contact method</legend>
  <input type="radio" id="email" name="contact" value="email">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input type="radio" id="phone" name="contact" value="phone">
  <label for="phone">Phone</label>
</fieldset>

quizData.question: Why use `<fieldset>` for a group of radio buttons?

options.text: To provide a group label announced by screen readers

quizData.explanation: The `<legend>` gives context to each option, so users know what they're selecting.

slides.title: Error Handling & Validation ❗
slides.content:
When errors occur:

* Announce them with `aria-live` regions (more in Chapter 5).
* Associate error messages with the field using `aria-describedby`.
* Use clear, plain language – explain how to fix the error.

For now, just ensure labels are always there. We'll cover ARIA later.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test Your Forms
Try filling a form using only the keyboard. Can you navigate logically? Do you always know what each field is for?
